metadata.title: Quantitative Systems Pharmacology (QSP)-Based Dose Selection for Minimum Anticipated Biological Effect Level (MABEL) in First-in-Human (FIH) Trials

candidates.statement: In general, FDA’s guidance documents do not establish legally enforceable responsibilities. 35 Instead, guidances describe the Agency’s current thinking on a topic and should be viewed only 36 as recommendations, unless specific regulatory or statutory requirements are cited. The use of 37 the word should in Agency guidances means that something is suggested or recommended, but 38 not required. 39
candidates.context: The focus of this guidance is on drugs for which the MABEL approach is recommended to guide 30 starting doses for FIH trials. This can, but does not necessarily, include drugs that cause T-cell 31 activation and subsequent cytokine release. Here, we provide recommendations for leveraging 32 mechanistic QSP as a model-based approach to improve FIH dose estimation. 33

candidates.context: QSP provides a framework to integrate mechanistic understanding and diverse data into a 80 predictive model. For a MABEL-based FIH dose, the primary goal of the QSP model is to 81 estimate a dose that is expected to result in a minimal but measurable biological effect in 82 humans. 83 • Integration of All Available Data : A foundational principle for QSP modeling is to 88 consider all relevant data for dose prediction. candidates.statement: • Model Verification : Sponsors should conduct verification procedures to confirm that the 202 model equations and coding implementations are free of errors, such as incorrect 203 calculations or inconsistent units. Sponsors should verify basic model behaviors during 204 initial checks. For example, sponsors should ensure that the absence of drug 205 administration results in no pharmacological effect and that sufficiently high drug doses 206 lead to target saturation. For stochastic models, sponsors should verify stochastic stability 207 to ensure consistent and realistic variability across simulations. 208
candidates.context: • Code Development : Sponsors should develop the QSP model using reliable 199 computational software and document the code thoroughly. 200 • Model Calibration and Validation : Sponsors should thoroughly document the calibration 210 process, including methods, rationale for parameter adjustments, and the resulting 211 alignment with observed data to ensure transparency. candidates.statement: • Sensitivity and Uncertainty Analyses : Sponsors should conduct sensitivity analyses to 229 systematically determine how changes in individual model parameters influence 230 predictions and dosing recommendations. Sponsors should address model structural 231 uncertainty by evaluating alternative biological hypotheses and model architectures. 232 Sponsors should quantify how collective knowledge gaps, both in parameter estimates 233 and underlying biological assumptions or model structures, affect the overall confidence 234 in model predictions. These analyses help identify parameters and/or structure 235 assumptions with the greatest impact on outcomes and evaluate the robustness of dose 236 recommendations across realistic parameter and model structure variations. Sponsors 237 should thoroughly communicate the impact of the model parameters and/or structure 238 assumptions on the robustness of the proposed FIH dose to ensure transparency. 239
candidates.context: • Model Application : After successful validation, the model can be applied to predict the 220 drug responses under different dosing regimens. This can lead to the prediction of the 221 FIH dose and potential suggestions for dose-escalation increments. Specifically, 222 simulating pharmacological responses at multiple low-dose levels surrounding the 223 anticipated starting dose can help visualize the steepness or shallowness of the dose- 224 response relationship. candidates.statement: − In general, sponsors should err on the side of caution when selecting the FIH 245 starting dose for the safety of the clinical trial participants. Additional caution is 246 warranted when a QSP-based dose differs substantially from traditional MABEL 247 estimates (those using in vitro pharmacology activity and binding studies 248 conducted with the investigational product). In such cases, sponsors should 249 demonstrate the model’s reliability, ideally through retrospective validation using 250 clinical outcomes from compounds with a similar mechanism of action (and 251 structure, as applicable). 252

candidates.statement: When applying a QSP approach for dose selection in a FIH trial, sponsors should submit a QSP 303 Study Report and provide documentation of methods, assumptions or uncertainties, and other 304 information recommended in this guidance. Early interaction between sponsors and the Agency 305 can improve model development and subsequent planning of FIH trial design. Specific 306 development-related discussions can be helpful to ensure full alignment on the risk-based 307 assessment, technical details on QSP modeling and evaluation, and approaches for 308 implementation in clinical trial design. The mechanisms described below can be considered for 309 sponsor engagement with the Agency. 310
